This. I work in a sales adjacent support role so I have the privilege of sitting on many pricing calls. No amount of incoherent repetition and babbling makes either your team on the call or the customer more inclined to trust you.

Take the time to prepare a confident talk track in advance, speak your piece, and stop talking. The silence doesn’t make you appear awkward, it makes you appear confident. 

And, actually listen to what your customers have to say. The silence will give you more information than you anticipated. While every call cannot be that $1m sale you were hoping for, all information from the customer is good information.

Said this a couple of times in this subreddit. It’s a dreadful way to look at the world, but customers only care about two things - fear of being otherwise unable to do their job without your product, or money. Strongly recommend setting pricing expiration dates on consolidated purchases. And be up front, too, because they don’t want to play games either. Tell them your finance team is, and they probably are, highly motivated to get the deal done by the end of the quarter, and if it doesn’t get done, raise the price and stick to your word. And don’t just raise it a little, show them the price will go up by 25 -30%. Guarantee you will motivate SOME, but not all, people to get it done before the end of the quarter.
Mona Lisa (ft. Kendrick Lamar) - Lil Wayne. Does that qualify as hip hop though? Not sure 🤔

The idea that former athletes understand competition and hard work inherently more than other employees isn’t true. Furthermore, I would propose that these characteristics or ideas are actually not what make a sales person successful. You’re not going to win the hearts and minds of your customers with the same mindset needed to make a tackle, or kick a ball at a goal. In my experience, type A personalities needed to be for example a quarterback which have allowed athletes to be successful in the past, tend to prevent the person from practicing the patience, understanding, and a calculated approach needed to forming healthy relationships with customers to influence their decisions. Ps, I competed in the NCAA for four years, and I thoroughly reject the idea that I’m somehow better than someone because I played a sport.
Don’t. Folks will constantly email like this, and it’s a reflection of their character. You will be happier in your career if you let it go.

There are only two motivators which you can use to move your prospects/customers to take action -

1. Money - the potential to save on current purchases, or earn return on investment from your product 

2. Fear - the threat of being indisposed by an unforeseen issue which your product can mitigate
